propositions: The parent-first cascade logic is duplicated in claim.py and transition.py, with identical ghost/init preconditions but distinct write primitives and cascading-edge tables

The consolidation extracts only the walk (recursion, cycle guard, TOCTOU re-check, error rewrap) into a shared module, leaving the decision table (_CASCADING_EDGES) and write primitives at their original sites
Three cascading edges exist (open→in_progress, closed→open, closed→in_progress) but claim only supports one; the extraction must preserve all three without silent regression
The inbound reconciler from Gerrit 2044 already single-sources the decision by importing _CASCADING_EDGES and must keep its own write primitive and topmost-first ordering guarantee
A parametrised test over _CASCADING_EDGES (not hand-enumerated per-edge cases) is required to prevent future 'unknown edge' regressions like cranial-sulfur-peafowl and paragonite-fruited-minnow
